title: Release tooling: generate provenance metadata for offline bundles + reference in manifest
author: Devon Price
release_notes: Offline bundle manifests now include references to build provenance metadata (commit SHAs, CI build identifiers, builder image digest) to improve auditability for air-gapped installs.
description: Context: As part of signed offline bundles for air-gapped Redwood Private installs, we need traceability from a bundle back to the exact source + CI run that produced it. This PR adds a provenance metadata generator in the release tooling and wires it into offline bundle manifest generation as a referenced artifact. Summary of changes: (1) Generate a `provenance.json` file during bundle build containing repo/commit SHAs, build/run identifiers, and builder environment identifiers. (2) Store provenance as a standalone artifact in the bundle directory and include its digest + relative path in the bundle manifest (manifest does not embed large provenance payloads). (3) Make output deterministic by default: stable JSON encoding, sorted keys/arrays, no wall-clock timestamps unless explicitly provided by CI, and normalized paths. Motivation: Regulated customers require auditable provenance that can be validated fully offline; this also supports future CI attestation linkage without changing the bundle format. Testing: added unit tests for deterministic output and golden fixtures for a sample bundle; ran `tools/release` integration test target locally + in CI. Notes: this PR intentionally does not implement signing/verification; that is handled in the signing-stage PR and installer verification work.
commits: tools/release/offline_bundle: include provenance reference + digest in bundle manifest
tests: add deterministic encoding tests + golden fixtures
docs: developer notes for CI env vars used for build IDs
conversation: Connor O'Brien (review): Can you clarify whether provenance will be embedded into the manifest or referenced? I want to avoid the manifest ballooning over time as we add more fields (SBOM pointers, etc.).

Devon Price (author): Referenced. This PR writes `provenance.json` next to `bundle.manifest.json` and includes only `{path, sha256, mediaType, schemaVersion}` in the manifest under `provenanceRef`. The installer can verify the digest and (later) optionally display/emit the provenance content for audit exports.

Sahana Iyer (review): Determinism concern: `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True)` is not enough if we include arrays that might come from filesystem traversal. Also please don't include `generated_at` timestamps unless they come from CI and are normalized (we saw this bite reproducible builds before).

Devon Price (author): Good call. Updated to: (a) explicit sorting for arrays (`git_commits`, `inputs`, `artifacts`) (b) canonical path normalization and stable ordering of env-derived fields (c) removed `generated_at` completely; if CI wants a timestamp later we can pass `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and record it as `build.sourceDateEpoch` (integer). Added a determinism test that runs generation twice with shuffled input ordering and asserts byte-for-byte equality.

Marcus Lin (security review): Please make sure we are not implying any trust in provenance by itself. It should be integrity-protected only when the bundle signature covers it. Also include the builder image digest / tool version so auditors can see what produced it.

Devon Price (author): Agreed. The provenance doc explicitly states: 'not a signature/attestation; informational unless covered by a verified bundle signature'. Added `builder.imageDigest` (if present via CI) + `tooling.version` (from `git describe` fallback) and `tooling.commit` (for the release tooling itself).

Kevin Osei (review): From an audit/export standpoint, can we ensure the provenance includes both the monorepo commit and the subcomponent commits for any vendored artifacts? Also, please keep IDs consistent across CI providers; some customers will request evidence that references a stable build id.

Devon Price (author): Added fields: `source.repo`, `source.commit`, and `components[]` entries when the bundle builder is given per-component commit pins (e.g., helm charts, installer). For CI identifiers: we now emit `build.provider` + `build.runId` + `build.runUrl` when available; for local builds these are omitted. All optional fields are excluded (not null) to keep encoding stable.
Sahana Iyer (follow-up): I still see `platform.node` (hostname) in the provenance. That will vary per runner and breaks determinism even in CI.

Devon Price (author): Removed hostname + any machine-specific identifiers. Kept only `platform.os`, `platform.arch`, and `platform.python` (tool runtime) since those should be stable per CI image and useful for debugging. Updated golden fixture accordingly.

Connor O'Brien (approval): Looks good now. The determinism tests + omission of wall-clock timestamps address the concern. Please link this PR from the signing-stage PR so the relationship is obvious during release reviews.
Devon Price (author): Added cross-link in the signing-stage PR description and referenced ENG-3916 in both.

Marcus Lin (approval): Approved with the current wording + removal of machine identifiers. Follow-up: once the signing PR lands, we should ensure the signature covers `provenance.json` (it will if it's part of the bundle manifest digest set).
